facts.fact: Orbicularis oris is an annular complex around the mouth; older descriptions called it a sphincter, but later work found its fibers run in different directions and it is composed of four quadrants that interlace to give an appearance of circularity (not a uniform circular sphincter). Source: Wikipedia/Radiopaedia results aggregated in the orbicularis oris search.
The orbicularis oris has an outer marginal part and an inner labial part.

Lower-lip supplementary orbicularis fibers include a slip of m. incisivus labii inferioris on each side of the midline arising from the mandible, fibers from the buccinator and caninus, and deep fibers from the modiolus.
Motor innervation of orbicularis oris is by the buccal branch of the facial nerve (CN VII); superior and inferior labial arteries run between the muscle fibers and mucosa.
Depressor anguli oris (DAO) is a triangular muscle at the mouth corner; fibers originate from the lower jaw along the oblique line and converge to insert into the modiolus.
In a cadaver study, the DAO modiolus insertion was reported about 10 mm lateral and 10 mm caudal to the oral commissure.
Mentalis originates from the anterior mandible (mental protuberance near midline) and inserts into the skin of the chin; its motor supply is the marginal mandibular branch of CN VII.

Sources disagree on the exact bony origin of the mentalis: StatPearls Mandible lists the incisive fossa, while the Italian consensus review describes origin from the alveolar bone of the anterior mandible.
Depressor labii inferioris (DLI) originates from the mandible and inserts into the lower lip; it is supplied solely by the marginal mandibular branch in a fresh-cadaver dissection of ten hemifaces.
The platysma's middle portion (pars labialis) crosses the body of the mandible, continues under the DAO, and inserts into the lower lip dermis and orbicularis oris.

A cadaveric study (Bae et al., as reported in search results) found the anterior platysma ascends to interdigitate with the DAO and DLI, and the lower one-third of the masseter is covered by the platysma.
Minelli et al. (2022) found the jowl is a localized area of redundant skin and subcutaneous fat, and its anterior border is not defined by a specific osteocutaneous structure.

The mandibular ligament is described (2022 study) as existing only in the deep, sub-platysma plane, formed by combined muscular attachment to the mandible of the lower lip depressor muscles and the platysma.
A 2018 layered-anatomy study attributed jowl deformity to loose platysma adherence to the mandible, occurring posterior but not anterior to the mandibular ligament.
A 2025 cadaver study in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery reported a conjoined mass and a tissue band from the modiolus to the dermis, classed as a 'false ligament'; this is a single small study.
Radiopaedia describes the modiolus as a small fibromuscular structure at the mouth corner where fibers from multiple facial muscles converge (it cites nine muscles' fibers joining at the commissure).
Named contributors to the modiolus include orbicularis oris, levator and depressor anguli oris, risorius, platysma, buccinator and zygomaticus major; sources differ on the exact count.

Facial artery supplies the modiolus region, branching into inferior and superior labial arteries; in a dissection of five cadavers the facial artery lay anterior to the modiolus in 1 specimen (20%) and lateral in 4 (80%), never medial.

A 2025 ultrasound study of 45 young and 45 elderly Asian adults found a statistically significant downward and inward shift of the modiolus with age, attributed to laxity of lip elevators and contracture of lip depressors.
A 2025 micro-CT study reports the labiomandibular fold is accentuated with age by downward pull of depressor muscles (DAO, platysma, buccinator fibers).
A December 2025 review argues chronic shortening and increased resting tone of facial muscles alter form and function, describing hypertonic DAO as a secondary contributor to lip aging.

In a cadaver and ultrasound study of the mentalis, measured 5 mm lateral to the chin's most prominent point, depth was 6.7 ± 1.4 mm, bone-to-muscle distance 1.1 ± 1.0 mm, and muscle thickness 4.0 ± 1.4 mm (units mm; reported as cited in the search summary, not verified against full text).
A technical report describes the mentalis as spanning roughly 5-10 mm in the sagittal midline and 20-30 mm horizontally (per search summary; primary source not confirmed).

Choi et al. (Aesthetic Surgery Journal, 2021), 45 embalmed cadavers, reported soft-tissue (skin plus subcutaneous) thickness of 6.4 mm (SD 1.7) at the DLI reference point; this is not muscle thickness.
A 2021 ultrasound study of Caucasian patients reported an average DAO depth of 3.1 mm and DLI overlap in 12% of patients, versus under 5% in cadaveric dissection data.

Onabotulinumtoxin A injection into the mentalis in 11 patients with underprojected chin and high-riding hyperactive mentalis: chin point moved downward in 10 of 11 patients; dimpling reduced on frontal photos.
Published mentalis BoNT doses vary: 4 U per side under ultrasound, and 12-15 U total in the measurement study.
A 2026 review notes the evidence does not justify increasing mentalis dose solely on muscle thickness when the goal is reducing chin dimpling.

A chin ptosis review recommends standardized assessment at rest and during animation, including mentalis function, skeletal projection, submental crease and cervicomental angle; inadequate reattachment of the mentalis to the anterior mandible after surgery can cause bunching or dimpling of chin skin.

Chin dimpling mechanism: mentalis dermal insertions can pull skin inward; a McGill explainer says chin dimples are unrelated to muscle, while a plastic surgeon commentary argues central dimples reflect soft-tissue muscle defects. Sources disagree.
Wikipedia's dimple article notes that Professor John McDonald, citing limited research, concluded dimples were mislabeled as genetically inherited and dominant.
A 2010 study of 500 Yoruba Nigerians with cheek dimples found 36 (7.2%) also had cleft chin; this is a subgroup figure among cheek-dimple carriers, not a general cleft chin prevalence.
Lower lip droop is listed as a possible adverse event of chin BoNT injection, requiring careful placement.

Misplaced BoNT in the mentalis can spread to DLI (speech difficulty) or orbicularis oris (incompetent lip or asymmetry); a separate review says diffusion does not often affect these muscles. Sources disagree on frequency.
Deep mentalis injection alone may be insufficient for chin dimpling because dimpling arises from mentalis fibers attaching to chin skin.

Marionette-line treatment: BoNT into the DAO (often with filler) is an established adjunct; a split-face study used 4 U into the DAO on one side and a prospective study reported median mouth-corner droop improved from -4 degrees to -1 degree at 2 weeks and 3 months after filler plus incobotulinumtoxinA into DAO and mentalis.
Evidence for DAO-BoNT in marionette lines is mostly small studies, case reports and expert opinion; reviews call for larger multicenter trials.
Depressor labii inferioris palsy has been reported after chin augmentation (2024 case report), illustrating the muscle's vulnerability in chin procedures.
Fetal histology study (2024) examined growth patterns of facial muscles at the mouth angle in midterm and near-term fetuses.

contradictions: Orbicularis oris: older texts call it a sphincter; later work says its fibers run in differing directions as four interlacing quadrants.
Mentalis origin: StatPearls Mandible says incisive fossa; the Italian consensus review says alveolar bone of anterior mandible.
Modiolus muscle count: Radiopaedia cites nine muscles; other summaries list six to eight, and one adds zygomaticus minor.
Chin dimple mechanism: McGill says muscle-unrelated; a plastic surgeon commentary says soft-tissue muscle defect.
BoNT spread to DLI/orbicularis oris: one review calls it a real risk for speech and lip competence; another says it rarely affects these muscles.
Mentalis dimensions: a technical report gives 5-10 mm sagittal and 20-30 mm horizontal, which were not checked against a primary measurement.
DLI overlap: 12% in ultrasound vs under 5% in cadaver dissection.
openQuestions: No population prevalence figure for chin cleft or chin dimple was found; an epidemiological or anthropometric search is needed.
Full-text numbers for mentalis thickness (cadaver and ultrasound) were only seen as search summaries; the primary tables were not fetched.
A true DLI muscle-thickness measurement was not found; the Choi 2021 figure is soft tissue, not muscle.
The 2008 five-cadaver modiolus dissection and the 2025 false-ligament cadaver study need full-text verification.
Blender-specific sculpting references for the lower face were not found; GitHub results were developer notes only.
Bae et al. platysma cadaver study citation details (journal, year) were not confirmed.
Fetal histology (PubMed 38953435) results were not read beyond the title.
